messages:
sara_cs: FYI customer reported sudden 200-400ms extra latency and intermittent 401s this morning. Tenant is EU-ACME (eu-west-1). We see a hosted billing spike for the same tenant. Can someone look?

sara_cs: core details: requests claim X-Region: eu-west-1 but routing shows pool=hosted-us-1 in trace. Logs attached (snippet below).

sara_cs: ```TRACE: req=abc123 route_decision=hosted-us-1 pool_capacity=94% ttl_sticky=0 tenant=eu-acme auth=401 sometimes
header:X-Region=eu-west-1
```

michael_infra: thanks — sending to infra oncall. @olivia_oncall can you grab routing logs for tenant eu-acme between 08:12-08:40 UTC? need request_ids + decision reasons.

olivia_oncall: grabbing logs now. quick q: is this only for generation endpoints or embeddings too?

sara_cs: customer saw it on generation (completions) and their billing shows tokens on hosted SKU. embeddings look fine so far.

ben_platform: jumping in — two likely suspects: (1) sticky-affinity TTL expiration logic, (2) tie-breaker fallback picks wrong cluster tag when dedicated pool >90% capacity. We shipped a change last month that prefers lowest-latency fallback cluster but a metadata key bug can compare region tag incorrectly.

ben_platform: repro I saw: when dedicated pool capacity crosses threshold and no regional backup available, tie-breaker compares "pool.region" vs request.X-Region but uses canonical tag "eu" vs "eu-west-1" -> mismatch -> falls back to global hosted.

olivia_oncall: collected logs: found 3k hits where decision_reason=FALLBACK_TIE_BREAKER and chosen_pool=hosted-us-1. request_ids sample: abc123, def456, ghi789. copying snippet: ```decision=FALLBACK_TIE_BREAKER chosen=hosted-us-1 compare(left=eu-west-1,right=eu)```

esc_ops: oh — that would also explain auth 401s: auth proxy issues tokens scoped to eu-cluster; when routed to hosted-us, token audience mismatch -> 401. billing spike explained by fallback to hosted SKU.

michael_infra: thanks. can we repro locally? steps?

ben_platform: repro steps I used:
1) create dedicated pool sim with region tag "eu" and simulate capacity 92%
2) send requests with header `X-Region: eu-west-1` and tenant eu-acme
3) observe decision logs: fallback chosen=hosted-us-1 due to tag mismatch

ben_platform: quick curl example:
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Region: eu-west-1" -H "X-Tenant: eu-acme" \\  -d '{"prompt":"test"}' https://inference.example/api/v1/generate
```

olivia_oncall: I can repro in staging when I artificially set pool.capacity=0.92 and the pool.tag=eu (while request header uses eu-west-1). Confirmed fallback to global-hosted path.

esc_ops: immediate mitigation options? customer is on Dedicated contract. they need their traffic routed to eu-hosted backup or stay queued in dedicated.

ben_platform: short term: push a forced-route rule for tenant eu-acme to regional backup (eu-hosted) or deny fallback to global-hosted while we hotfix. I'll open an emergency policy override.

michael_infra: doing policy override now -> adding rule: tenant:eu-acme prefer_pool_tag:eu-west-1 allow_fallback:false.

deploy-bot: deployment queued: policy-update/override-2012345678 -> started, estimated 2m.

olivia_oncall: after override, customer latency back to normal and no 401s for a 30m window. Billing spike stabilized.

ben_platform: root cause: tag canonicalization mismatch between pool metadata and request region header; tie-breaker fallback used non-canonical tag. We'll land hotfix in runtime comparator: normalize tags (eu, eu-west-1, eu-west) and prefer regional backup pool when tenant dedicated exists.

ben_platform: action items: 1) hotfix comparator (PR opened #4678), 2) add integration test for tag normalization, 3) audit all tenant overrides for similar regressions, 4) add alert when FALLBACK_TIE_BREAKER % > 1% per tenant.

esc_ops: assigned follow-ups to platform + infra. I'll update customer with timeline and mitigation note. :thumbsup: 

sara_cs: customer update: told them we applied temporary routing override and working on hotfix; they appreciated quick fix. Closing escalation if no further anomalies.

michael_infra: closing loop — will watch for regressions overnight, flag if any recurrence.

sara_cs: thanks team :raised_hands:
